We cut the old material out, clean the channel and re-fill it so the slab can move without letting anything in. 08 Asphalt & blacktop sealing → Sealed and conditioned with a natural-oil product containing no asphalt and no tar. Old blacktop is restored rather than painted over. Why concrete fails in southern Utah Concrete does not crack because it is weak. 01 It moves. Concrete expands and contracts with temperature: roughly 5.5 millionths of an inch, per inch, per degree Fahrenheit. Swing a 50-foot driveway 100°F between a January night and a July afternoon and that is about a third of an inch of movement. The slab is pinned by the ground under it and whatever it butts against, so the movement turns into stress, and stress opens hairline cracks. Control joints exist to choose where. 02 It drinks. Concrete is porous. Water wicks into the capillary pores and down into every crack the movement just opened, and it carries whatever is dissolved in it. Salt off the pool. Salt out of the softener. Salt already in the soil and the hard water it came from. 03 Then it breaks from the inside. Water expands about nine percent when it freezes, and southern Utah nights do drop below freezing. A saturated pore has nowhere to put that. Salt does the same job without needing the cold. As water evaporates the salt crystallises, and crystals growing inside a confined pore push hard enough to lift the surface off. Scaling, spalling, and the white bloom of efflorescence are all the same story. Sealing does not stop concrete moving. Nothing does. What it stops is water being there to take advantage of the movement. Keep the pore network from staying saturated and you starve both freeze–thaw and salt crystallisation of the one thing they need. Movement on its own is just movement. Our concrete sealing process Four steps. No shortcuts in any of them. 01 Clean The slab gets cleaned end to end. Nothing goes down over dirt. 02 Dry We wait for it to dry completely. Sealer over moisture is how finishes fail. 03 Seal Deco product, matched to the surface and the exposure it lives in. 04 Cure Twenty-four hours before you walk or drive on it. Then it is yours again. 24 hours That is the honest answer to the question everyone actually asks: how long am I without my driveway? One day. We would rather tell you up front than have you find out on the way to work. Materials We only use Deco products. Deco Products has manufactured in Denver since 1991, water-based and solvent-free from the start. We are a certified Deco applicator, which is what lets us put down the restricted products, including the ICC-approved foundation membrane. No house-brand substitutions, no whatever was on the truck. So we offer a standing arrangement instead. We come back on a two-year cycle, clean it, and put a fresh coat down. You do not book it and you do not think about it, and the slab never gets far enough gone to need restoring. The high-shine finishes are a different conversation, because those do leave a layer on the surface. If you want a wet look somewhere that gets walked on barefoot and wet, say so at the assessment and we will talk it through rather than just quoting it. Will it change the colour? Wet-look and decorative finishes deliberately deepen the colour and lift the aggregate. That is the entire point of them. We will show you the difference on your own concrete before anything is committed to. Can you seal brand-new concrete? Not immediately. Fresh concrete has to cure and give up its moisture first, and sealing over that is how finishes fail early. If you are mid build, talk to us at the pour and we will schedule it properly. pool_deck_sealing.meta: Pool deck sealing in St. George, Utah with Salt Shield 303, a penetrating sealer that stops salt crystallisation without changing the slip resistance of the deck. Free on-site assessment.
pool_deck_sealing.text: id="top"> Armour Crete / Pool deck sealing Salt is eating your pool deck. Salt-water pools are everywhere in southern Utah, and so is the damage they leave on the concrete around them. We seal pool decks with a penetrating product built for exactly this, and it does not change how the deck feels under wet, bare feet. 0 Change to skid or slip resistance (manufacturer stated) Clear No film, no residue, no shine unless you ask for it 24h Cure before the deck is back in use Free On-site assessment, no obligation Why pool decks fail The damage happens inside the pore. Salt dissolves in splash-out and spray, soaks into the pores of the concrete, and then the desert does the rest: the water evaporates, the salt crystallises, and crystals growing inside a confined pore push hard enough to lift the surface right off the slab. That is the flaking and pitting you see in a ring around older pools. It is not wear; it is crystal pressure from the inside. Water-softener discharge does the same thing to whatever slab it drains onto, which is why we look at more than the pool surround when we come out. The fix is to keep the saltwater out of the pore network in the first place. A penetrating sealer blocks the water and the chlorides riding in it, without laying anything on the surface. What goes on it Salt Shield 303 exists for this. What each Deco product does → Clear silane/siloxane emulsion that penetrates deep into the slab Does not change the skid or slip resistance of the concrete Reduces spalling, freeze–thaw damage, dusting and mildew Non-hazardous, non-toxic, non-flammable It is a penetrating sealer, not a coating, so it does not make a wet deck slicker than it already was. High-shine finishes are a different conversation, because those do leave a layer; if you want a wet look somewhere that gets walked on barefoot and wet, say so at the assessment and we will talk it through rather than just quoting it. Travertine & stone surrounds Not all decks are concrete. Travertine is everywhere around southern Utah pools, and it stains in ways that do not come back out. Stone that will not absorb a penetrating sealer gets treated with a bonded acrylic made for non-porous surfaces ( TravaCast ), which guards against staining and discolouration on travertine, Spanish tile and stone coping. Which product your deck needs is exactly what the assessment decides. Pool deck questions Asked beside every pool. Will the deck be slippery afterwards? Not with Salt Shield 303. It soaks into the concrete and dries clear with no film on top, and the manufacturer states plainly that it does not change the skid or slip resistance of the surface. My deck is already flaking. Is it too late? Usually not, but the surface has to be corrected before any sealer goes down, because sealing over damage locks the damage in. That is a crack repair and restoration conversation first, and it is exactly what the free assessment is for. How long before the deck is back in use? Twenty-four hours. Plan for one day around the pool rather than on it. Does softener discharge really matter? Yes. It is the same salt mechanism in a different spot. The slab your softener drains onto is quietly running the same experiment as your pool deck, so we check it while we are there. Get started Request an assessment. We come out, look at the surface, and tell you what it needs. No charge for the visit, and no obligation attached to it. heads: The colour it haswhen it rains.
wet_look_concrete_sealing.text: id="top"> Armour Crete / Wet-look & decorative The colour it has when it rains. A wet-look finish deepens the colour of concrete, pavers or stone and holds it there: the way the surface looks in the first minute of a storm, kept. There are two honest ways to get there, and they age very differently, so we show you both on your own concrete before you choose. 2 Ways to a wet look: from within, or as a shine on top UV Protection in both, because the desert sun is the main event Demo Shown on your own surface before you commit Free On-site assessment, no obligation The honest distinction From within, or on top. SilaCast BES deepens the material's own colour from below. It penetrates porous surfaces (concrete pavers, roof and barrel tile, natural stone) rather than laying a film on top, it carries two forms of UV protection, and it never needs stripping before it can be re-coated. A topical film can yellow under UV, it can peel, and taking one off means harsh chemicals; a penetrating enhancer has none of those problems, because there is no film to fail. Shine-A-Cast is the other road: a hybrid that penetrates to enhance colour and also leaves a protective layer on the surface. That layer is what produces the high shine, what locks joint sand in place on paver work, and what brings a sun-faded surface back. Pigment can even be added to tune the colour. It is restricted to approved applicators, which we are. Which one belongs on your property depends on the surface, the sun it takes, and how you use it. A high-shine layer next to a pool is a conversation about slip resistance before it is a conversation about looks. Where it earns its keep Made for feature surfaces. Paver driveways and entries: colour up, joint sand locked Decorative patios and courtyards Exposed aggregate the builder got right, lifted rather than hidden Sun-faded surfaces that need their colour back Roof tile and retaining walls, enhanced from within If you want protection with no change in appearance at all, that is a different product doing a quieter job. See driveway sealing . Decorative sealing questions Decided at the demo. How dark will it go? That depends on the surface: how porous it is and what colour is already in it. Which is exactly why we demo it on your own concrete first: you see the actual result, not a brochure's version of it. Will it yellow in the sun? Yellowing is a film problem, and it is why we lean on penetrating products where they fit. SilaCast enhances from within the substrate and carries two types of UV protection; Shine-A-Cast's surface layer is UV protected as well. What we will not do is put down a bargain acrylic film and let the desert have it. How long before I can use the surface? Plan for twenty-four hours, the same as any sealing work we do. expansion_joint_replacement.title: Expansion Joint Replacement | St. George UT | Armour Crete
expansion_joint_replacement.meta: Concrete expansion joint replacement in St. George and Washington County. Failed joint filler lets water into the sub-base. We cut it out, clean the channel and re-fill it properly.
heads: The joint is doingits job. The filler isn't.
Water under the slabis the expensive kind.
expansion_joint_replacement.text: id="top"> Armour Crete / Expansion joints The joint is doing its job. The filler isn't. Joints exist so the slab can move without cracking where it pleases. When the filler in them dries out, shrinks and splits, every joint becomes a drain running straight down into the sub-base your driveway is sitting on. We cut the old material out, clean the channel, and re-fill it so the slab can keep moving without letting anything in. 1/3" Roughly how much a 50-foot slab moves across our seasons 3 Steps: cut out, clean, re-fill. No caulk over the top of failure Free On-site assessment, no obligation Why it matters Water under the slab is the expensive kind. Concrete expands and contracts with temperature, and southern Utah gives it a hundred-degree annual swing to work with. The joints are where that movement is supposed to happen. But movement is exactly what kills the filler: it stretches and compresses season after season until it pulls away from the joint walls or splits down the middle. After that, every storm and every sprinkler cycle sends water through the open joint into the sub-base, the compacted material the slab depends on. Wash enough of it out and the slab settles, rocks and cracks, and at that point the repair is no longer a joint repair. Re-filling a failed joint costs a fraction of correcting a settled slab. It is also the first thing we check before sealing a driveway , because sealing the surface while the joints are open is solving the small leak and ignoring the big one. How we do it Out, clean, and back in. The failed filler is cut out completely, not topped up or caulked over The channel is cleaned back to sound edges so the new material can bond The joint is re-filled with material that flexes with the slab's movement Done alongside sealing or on its own, whichever the surface actually needs Filler that is simply laid over the top of failed material fails again on the same schedule. Cutting it out is slower. It is also the job. Expansion joint questions Worth asking before it settles. How do I know my joints have failed? Look along them. Filler that has sunk below the surface, pulled away from either edge, cracked down its length or gone hard and crumbly is no longer keeping water out. Weeds growing out of a joint are the surface's way of filing a report. Can you just fill the gaps that look bad? We can, but we will tell you what we see first. Joint filler tends to age at the same rate across a slab, so one failed section usually means the rest are close behind, and doing them together costs less than doing them twice. Does this get done before or after sealing? Before. Prep first, always: joints, cracks and surface correction all come ahead of any sealer. Nothing goes down over a problem. asphalt_sealing.meta: Asphalt and blacktop sealing in St. George, Utah with Bio Blacktop: natural oils and co-polymers that condition dried-out asphalt rather than painting tar over it.
asphalt_sealing.text: id="top"> Armour Crete / Asphalt & blacktop Restored, not painted over. Almost every blacktop sealer on the market is an asphalt or tar product: a by-product of the oil industry, painted back onto your driveway. We use a blend of natural oils and co-polymers instead, so old grey asphalt gets its colour and its flexibility back rather than a coat of black paint. 0 Asphalt or tar in the product Fast Dry time, with soap-and-water cleanup UV And chemical resistant, built for full desert sun Free On-site assessment, no obligation Why asphalt goes grey The sun cooks the binder out. Asphalt is aggregate held together by a flexible binder, and the desert sun spends every summer drying that binder out. As it goes, the surface fades from black to grey, turns brittle, and starts shedding gravel; cracks follow, water gets in, and the freeze–thaw cycle finishes the argument. A dried-out driveway does not need painting. It needs its flexibility back. That is the difference between conditioning and coating. A tar emulsion lays a black film over the top; it looks new for a season, then wears through in the tyre tracks. A conditioner soaks in and feeds the binder itself, which is why the colour that comes back is the asphalt's own. What goes on it Bio Blacktop, sprayed and rolled. What each Deco product does → Natural oils and co-polymers, with no asphalt and no tar Conditions old, dried-out asphalt rather than coating it Chemical and UV resistant Dries fast, and cleans up with soap and water It gets sprayed and back-rolled, never squeegeed. A squeegee pulls too much material to the surface and you end up with a driveway that looks painted, which is the exact thing this product exists to avoid. Asphalt sealing questions The blacktop questions. Will it look wet-black like a tar coat? It brings back the asphalt's own colour: a rich dark surface rather than a painted-on gloss. If a driveway looks lacquered, that is a film sitting on top, and films on asphalt wear through exactly where you drive. My asphalt is cracked. Seal or repair first? Repair first, same rule as concrete: nothing goes down over a problem. What is worth repairing versus living with is exactly what the free assessment sorts out. How long before I can drive on it? It dries fast (faster than our concrete work), but plan around the day of application and we will give you the exact window when we see the surface. Get started Request an assessment. The desert does not wait long. Hundred-degree summer slabs, winter nights below freezing, salt pools and softener discharge all start working on an unsealed surface from year one. Out here the sun does most of the damage and the winter nights finish it. An exposed slab swings through more than a hundred degrees across the year; the movement opens hairline cracks, water and salt follow them in, and freeze–thaw plus salt crystallisation break the surface from the inside. Unsealed concrete in full exposure simply runs that cycle faster than concrete that gets any shade at all. A penetrating sealer keeps the pore network from staying saturated, which is the whole game. Clear penetrating sealers that leave the surface looking exactly as the architect intended, on driveways, patios, pool surrounds and the stone beside them. 100% Transparent. The clear penetrating sealer dries one hundred percent transparent: no film, no sheen, no sign it is there. Where a surface is meant to read richer, enhancement from within deepens the material's own colour without laying plastic over it. And travertine or stone around a pool gets its own product , because stone stains in ways that do not come back out. Red rock, red dust The desert is the view. It is also the problem. The same exposure that makes Ivins worth building in works on the concrete every day: hard UV, hundred-degree seasonal swings, winter nights below freezing, and the iron-red dust that finds its way into every open pore. A sealed surface gives the dust nowhere to lodge and the water nowhere to sit. The slab rinses clean instead of staining, and the freeze–thaw cycle is starved of the moisture it needs. On architectural concrete the prep matters as much as the product: cracks corrected, joints re-filled cleanly, and the sealer applied in the early morning before the slab takes on heat, because a flash-dried finish streaks, and on a surface this visible, streaks are the whole story. concrete_sealing_santa_clara_ut.text: id="top"> Armour Crete / Santa Clara, UT Concrete sealing in Santa Clara. Santa Clara has some of the oldest streets in the county and some of the newest, which means slabs at every stage of their life. The older ones usually need honest prep before anything goes down; the newer ones are at the perfect moment to be protected. We handle both. Prep First, always. Nothing goes down over a problem 24h Cure before the surface is back in use Free On-site assessment, anywhere in Santa Clara Services in Santa Clara, UT Everything we do, done here. Driveway sealing Pool deck sealing Wet-look & decorative Expansion joints Asphalt & blacktop Foundation waterproofing On the established streets the work often starts with correction: failed joints re-filled , cracks patched, surfaces cleaned back to sound concrete. Sealer over damage just locks the damage in. On the newer builds toward the hills it is the opposite job: young slabs, fully cured, sealed before the desert has taken anything from them. Older slabs, honest answers Restore what's worth restoring. Say so when it isn't. Decades of sun, sprinklers and winter nights leave their record in a slab: scaling at the edges, joints gone crumbly, the white bloom of efflorescence where water has been moving through. Most of it can be corrected and sealed, and the result is a surface that stops getting worse. Some of it is past that, and the honest call is replacement before protection. That call is what the free assessment is for. We tell you which side of the line your concrete is on, what the prep would involve, and what the sealed surface will and will not look like afterwards. On your own slab, not a brochure's. Santa Clara questions Asked in Santa Clara. Our driveway is thirty years old. Is sealing even worth it? Often, yes, once it has been corrected. If the surface is sound or can be made sound, sealing stops the decline where it is. If it is past saving we will say so plainly, because sealing a failed slab wastes your money and our name. Trees shade half our patio. Does that change anything? It changes the wear pattern. Shaded concrete and full-sun concrete age at very different rates, and organic debris holds moisture against the surface. Same four-step process, but the product choice and the maintenance cycle take the shade into account. How long before we can use the surface again? Twenty-four hours after the sealer goes down. products.title: Deco Concrete Sealers We Use | St. George, UT | Armour Crete
products.meta: The six Deco sealers Armour Crete applies in St. George, Utah: DECO 20 Clear, Salt Shield 303, SilaCast BES, Shine-A-Cast, TravaCast and Bio Blacktop. Penetrating vs topical, surfaces and coverage.
products.text: id="main" data-astro-cid-3swd3b6j> Materials We only use Deco products. Deco Products has been manufacturing in Denver since 1991, water-based and solvent-free from the start. We are a certified Deco applicator, which is what lets us put down the restricted products. Shine-A-Cast and the Deco 20 Seal foundation membrane are approved-applicator only. Which sealer goes on your property is decided by the surface, the exposure and the finish you want, not by what happened to be on the truck. 1991 Deco’s first product, still in the range ICC Approved for foundation dampproofing 0 Solvents, and no house-brand substitutions ✓ Deco Certified Applicator 01 DECO 20 Clear Finish Type Penetrating · reactive Surface Concrete Coverage 1,200–1,500 sq ft / 5 gal Driveways Walkways Patios Garage floors Roof tile The original, and still the default. A non-hazardous reactive sealer that soaks in rather than sitting on top, and dries 100% transparent: no film, no sheen, no sign it is there. It is the one we reach for on ordinary flatwork, and it is the product Deco built the company on back in 1991. 100% transparent, so it changes nothing about how the surface looks Sharply slows how fast mould and mildew come back after a wash The only clear sealer ICC-approved for dampproofing basement foundations Non-hazardous, water-based, no solvents It goes down early in the morning, before the slab has taken on the day’s heat. On a hot surface it flash-dries and leaves whiting and streaks. In southern Utah that is not a small detail: it is most of the job. 02 Salt Shield 303 Type Penetrating · silane/siloxane Surface Salt-exposed concrete Coverage 1,000–1,500 sq ft / 5 gal Pool decks Salt pool surrounds Softener discharge Driveways Sidewalks For pool decks, and anywhere else salt lands. A clear water-based silane/siloxane emulsion that penetrates deep into the slab to block water and the chlorides riding in it. Salt is the specific problem: it dissolves in water, soaks into the pores, then crystallises as that water evaporates, and crystals growing inside a confined pore push hard enough to break the surface apart from underneath. Does not change the skid or slip resistance of the concrete Dries clear, with no film and no residue Reduces spalling, freeze–thaw damage, dusting and mildew Non-hazardous, non-toxic, non-flammable This is the answer to the pool-deck question. It is a penetrating sealer, not a coating, so it does not make a wet deck slicker than it already was. 03 SilaCast BES Type Penetrating · polymer emulsion Surface Pavers, roof tile & stone Coverage 700–1,000 sq ft / 5 gal Paver driveways Stone patios Roof tile Retaining walls Wet look, without the film. Beauty Enhancing Sealer, a non-hazardous polymer emulsion for porous units: concrete pavers, roof and barrel tile, natural stone. It penetrates and deepens the material’s own colour from below rather than laying a shiny film on top, and it carries two forms of UV protection. Never needs stripping before it can be re-coated Enhances colour from within the substrate, not from a surface film Two types of UV protection Lowest coverage of the range, because porous units simply drink more Worth knowing the difference: a topical acrylic sits on the surface as a film. Films can yellow under UV, they can peel, and taking one off means harsh chemicals. This does not build a film, so none of that applies. 04 Shine-A-Cast Type Hybrid · penetrating + topical Surface High shine Coverage 750–1,250 sq ft / 5 gal Wet-look driveways Decorative patios Paver work Feature entries When you want it obvious. A hybrid: it penetrates to enhance the colour and also leaves a protective layer on the surface, which is what produces the high shine and what locks paver joint sand in place. It will bring a sun-faded surface back, and pigment can be added to tune the colour. Wet-look, high-shine finish Locks joint sand on paver work UV protected and scratch resistant Restricted to approved applicators This one leaves a surface layer, so for a pool deck or anywhere that gets walked on wet it is a conversation rather than a default. Salt Shield is usually the better call there. 05 TravaCast Type Topical · acrylic Surface Natural stone Coverage 750–1,250 sq ft / 5 gal Travertine Spanish tile Flagstone Stone coping For stone that will not absorb anything. A single-component acrylic built for non-porous materials (travertine, Spanish tile, natural stone) where a penetrating sealer has nothing to penetrate into. It bonds to the surface instead, and comes UV protected. Adheres to non-porous stone and tile that penetrating sealers cannot treat Strong chemical resistance, and holds up against water blushing Guards against most staining and helps prevent discolouration Self-levelling, though back-rolling while wet helps Travertine is everywhere around southern Utah pools, and it stains in ways that do not come back out. This is a topical acrylic, so it will need redoing more often than the penetrating products above. 06 Bio Blacktop Type Conditioner · natural oil & co-polymer Surface Asphalt Coverage Varies with asphalt condition Asphalt driveways Blacktop parking Private lanes Asphalt, without the tar. Almost every blacktop sealer on the market is an asphalt or tar-based product: a by-product of the oil industry, painted back onto your driveway. This is not that. It is a blend of natural oils and co-polymers that conditions dried-out asphalt as well as sealing it, so an old grey driveway gets its colour and its flexibility back rather than just getting painted over. Contains no asphalt and no tar Conditions old, dried-out asphalt rather than coating it Chemical and UV resistant Dries fast, and cleans up with soap and water It gets sprayed and back-rolled, never squeegeed. A squeegee pulls too much material to the surface and you end up with a driveway that looks painted. Coverage varies with surface condition and porosity. A rough, older or thirstier slab drinks more, so treat these as planning figures rather than promises. Every job gets a test section before the rest of it goes down. For builders Deco 20 Seal, on the foundation side. The waterproofing membrane we spray on new foundation walls is a hybrid acrylic resin for poured concrete, pre-cast, masonry and ICF forms. It goes on as one continuous coating with no seams to fail, it can be applied to damp walls, and it removes the need for 6 mil poly. 01 Approved by the International Code Council 02 Continuous coating, no seams 03 Goes on damp walls, footing to top of wall 04 Rated for hydrostatic pressure 05 Bridges non-structural cracks 06 Not asphalt-based Independently tested to ASTM C 1306 for hydrostatic pressure over cracks, C 836 for low-temperature flexibility, crack bridging and adhesion strength, D 2939 for water resistance, and E 96 for water vapour permeance. Not sure which That is our problem, not yours. You do not need to pick a product. We look at the surface, the exposure and what you want it to look like, and we bring the right one. privacy.text: id="top"> Armour Crete / Privacy Your privacy, in plain words. What this website collects, why, who handles it for us, and how to ask us to delete it. It is short, because we collect very little. Updated September 25, 2026 0 Personal details sold or rented, ever 1 Analytics tool (Google Analytics), and no advertising pixels Who we are Armour Crete is a concrete sealing and foundation waterproofing business based in St. George, Utah. This policy covers the website at www.armour-crete.com. When it says "we" or "us", it means Armour Crete. What you send us The assessment request form asks for your name, phone, email, the type of property, the surface, an address or area, and anything else you want to tell us. The contractor enquiry form asks for your company, name, phone, email, trade, the scope and volume of work, where it is, and your notes. We use those details to reply, arrange a visit and quote the work. Nothing else. If a form fails to send, your own email app opens with the message filled in, and nothing leaves your device until you press send. What the site records on its own Google Analytics counts visits: which pages are viewed, how you arrived (a search, a link, typing the address), your approximate location worked out from your IP address, and your device, browser and screen size. It sets two cookies, _ga and _ga_MYHF4YMJ3Y , so a returning visitor can be told apart from a new one. We read the reports to see which pages are useful. We do not use them to work out who you are. Our host keeps standard server logs (IP address, browser, the page requested and the time) to deliver the site and protect it from abuse. Who handles it for us A few outside services do part of the work, and each has its own privacy policy: Vercel hosts the website. Vercel's privacy notice Google Analytics (Google LLC) measures visits. How Google uses this data Google Fonts (Google LLC) serves the typefaces. Your browser fetches them from Google, which sees your IP address. FormSubmit receives form submissions and forwards them to our inbox. FormSubmit's privacy policy Google Workspace (Google LLC) runs our email, which is where form submissions and anything you email us are kept. Google's privacy policy Cookies The only cookies on this site are the two Google Analytics cookies above. There are no advertising cookies and no tracking pixels. You can block or clear cookies in your browser settings, or install Google's Analytics opt-out add-on . The site works the same either way. What we do not do We do not sell or rent your information, and we do not hand it to anyone for their own marketing. Sending an enquiry does not put you on a mailing list. How long we keep it Enquiries and emails stay in our inbox while they are useful for the job and our records: quotes, scheduling, invoices and questions about work we did. Google Analytics keeps visit data for the limited period set in our account, after which Google deletes it. Your choices You can ask what we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it. Email evans@armour-crete.com or call 435·994·5235 . We will do it, unless we have to keep a record of work we did for you (an invoice, for example). Children This site is for homeowners and businesses. It is not aimed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their information. Changes If what we collect changes, this page changes with it, and the date at the top moves.
